reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Croup barks with steeple; epiglottitis drools with thumbprint
No throat examination in suspected epiglottitis
Foreign body is sudden stridor in well toddler
reference.pathophysiology: Immature supraglottic cartilage collapses under inspiratory negative pressure (Venturi) in laryngomalacia, while viral subglottic oedema in fixed cricoid ring (narrowest paediatric segment historically funnel) amplifies croup obstruction.
additionalDifferentials: Croup versus epiglottitis by toxicity, drool and cough
Laryngomalacia versus vocal cord palsy (cry quality, birth or cardiac surgery)
Stridor versus wheeze by sound and phase
additionalInvestigations: Flexible nasendoscopy awake in stable stridor
Neck imaging only when airway safe (steeple, thumbprint adjuncts)
Rigid bronchoscopy for foreign body and airway diagnosis
